answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Call the terrace the capital, the quartz the age bonus, and the tide the compounding curve: only undivided terrace keeps the quartz, and the tide shows exactly how much a split loses. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
